candidates.attacker_control: The clearest remote path is XML content that the broker parses on behalf of a client: a queue or consumer using an XPATH selector causes JAXPXPathEvaluator.evaluate(Filterable) to take the message body (`m.getBodyAs(String.class)`) and parse it with the DocumentBuilder obtained from XmlProvider (`XPathExpression` static initialiser, line 48). The message body is fully attacker-controlled by any user able to SEND to the address. The selector itself can be installed by a user with queue-creation permission. Other XmlProvider consumers (broker.xml/bootstrap.xml parsing, artemis data import/export, schema validation) are operator-driven but inherit the same default.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: (1) The property is named `disableXxe`, and the expression deliberately treats a bare `-Dartemis.disableXxe` (empty value) as 'disable', which is consistent with an intentional opt-in/backward-compatibility default where XXE is enabled unless explicitly disabled; the snapshot may therefore reflect upstream design rather than an injected regression. (2) The second conjunct's default, `Boolean.FALSE.toString()`, reads as deliberate and the surrounding hardening code (including the internal-schema resource resolver) is complete, so I could not prove the default was changed. (3) `setXxeEnabled` has no callers left in the visible tree, but test sources are excluded from this snapshot, so this is inconclusive. (4) I confirmed the code path and parser construction in source, but could not consult upstream history, the fix commit, or any CVE record, and no code was executed.
candidates.impact: XML External Entity injection: when an attacker-influenced XML document is parsed, the broker can be made to resolve external entities, enabling blind disclosure of files readable by the broker process (existence/parse-error oracles), SSRF to internal endpoints (file/http URLs in entity system identifiers), and denial of service through entity expansion / external DTD fetching. The concrete remote reachability is bounded by the XPath-selector code path; severity depends on whether such selectors are in use and on what the broker process can reach.
candidates.prerequisites: The broker must parse an attacker-influenced XML document through an XmlProvider-created parser while the `artemis.disableXxe` property is not set (the default). For the remote JMS path: an XPATH selector/filter on a queue or consumer, and SEND permission on that address for a second (possibly less privileged) user. Deployments that do not use XPath selectors, or that set -Dartemis.disableXxe, are not exposed through that path.
candidates.root_cause: XmlProvider computes its static `xxeEnabled` flag from the `artemis.disableXxe` system property with a default of Boolean.FALSE: `xxeEnabled = !"".equals(System.getProperty(ARTEMIS_DISABLE_XXE_PROPERTY)) && !Boolean.parseBoolean(System.getProperty(ARTEMIS_DISABLE_XXE_PROPERTY, Boolean.FALSE.toString()))`. With the property absent (the normal case) this evaluates to true, so every hardening branch written as `if (!isXxeEnabled())` is skipped and the created DocumentBuilder/XMLInputFactory/SchemaFactory/TransformerFactory/Validator permit DOCTYPE declarations, external general/parameter entities and external DTD/schema access. A single default value therefore disables the whole XXE-hardening feature for all callers of XmlProvider.
candidates.title: XXE protections in XmlProvider are disabled by default, allowing external entity/DTD resolution when attacker-controlled XML is parsed (e.g. server-side XPath selector evaluation of message bodies)
candidates.trace: XmlProvider lines 61-62 set xxeEnabled=true by default -> isXxeEnabled() (line 64) returns true -> newDocumentBuilder (line 76, hardening block at 101-109 skipped), createXMLStreamReader (114-125, hardening at 117-122 skipped), newSchemaFactory (131-158, hardening/resolver at 140-155 skipped), newTransformer (160-169), newValidator (171-180) produce parsers with DTD support and external entity resolution active. XPathExpression static initialiser (lines 40-58) builds the shared DocumentBuilder through XmlProvider.newDocumentBuilder and hands it to JAXPXPathEvaluator; JAXPXPathEvaluator.evaluate(Filterable) (56-63) parses the message body as XML (65-77), so entity/DTD resolution happens inside the broker JVM when a selector is evaluated for routing/filtering.
candidates.unverified: Whether the XXE-enabled default is the upstream intent or an injected regression could not be established from the snapshot alone; the full set of reachable XmlProvider call sites (especially any endpoint that parses arbitrary client XML) was not exhaustively enumerated; no runtime proof of entity resolution was produced (execution is out of scope).
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (insecure default; possible injected hardening regression)

coverage_summary: Files covered by the source filter: 2078 files (binary/symlink/size filters removed none); the P1 relation index covers 2053 files (25 source files absent from the index, 22 omitted overall) and provides only syntax-level containment/call/inheritance candidates with no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or runtime reachability (50 017 unresolved calls). I searched/read across the modules that matter for the request: security and authentication (SecurityStoreImpl, ActiveMQJAASSecurityManager, ActiveMQBasicSecurityManager, Properties/InVMLDAP/Certificate/Guest/LDAP/Kubernetes/SCRAM login modules, ScramUtils/ScramServerFunctionalityImpl, PasswordMaskingUtil/DefaultSensitiveStringCodec/SecureHashProcessor, User, CompositeAddress), authorization enforcement (ServerSessionImpl, ActiveMQServerImpl, CheckType, HierarchicalObjectRepository/Match), management (ManagementServiceImpl, ArtemisRbacInvocationHandler, ArtemisMBeanServerGuard, QueueControlImpl, AddressControlImpl, ActiveMQServerControlImpl, AbstractControl), protocols (OpenWireConnection/AMQSession/OpenWireProtocolManager, AMQP AMQPConnectionCallback/AMQPSessionCallback/PlainSASL/ProtonHandler, STOMP StompConnection/VersionedStompFrameHandler, MQTT protocol manager/handlers), XML and parsing utilities (XmlProvider, XPathExpression/JAXPXPathEvaluator, XMLUtil, ObjectInputStreamWithClassLoader, JsonUtil), and the CLI/web components. All described relation-index hits were verified against source text; no index label was treated as a finding. I did not exhaustively review the journal/paging/storage internals, JMS/RA modules, large message converters, or the distribution/image scripts, and no code, tests, or scanners were executed.
limitations: No upstream/diff/reference copy of the repository was available, so an injected change could not be distinguished from long-standing upstream behavior by comparison; findings rest on internal consistency only.
The snapshot contains only main sources (test sources are absent), removing evidence such as tests that exercise XXE configuration defaults or removed authorization checks.

The P1 index is syntactic only (parse candidates, no data/control flow, no semantic resolution, 50 017 unresolved calls and 25 files unindexed); it cannot prove reachability or exploitability and was used purely for navigation.

No execution, compilation, static-analysis run, or exploit attempt was performed, so all mechanisms (including XXE entity resolution and the XPath message-body path) are inferred from source and not runtime-confirmed.

Coverage of very large components was necessarily selective: journal/paging/storage internals, JMS and resource-adapter code, protocol message converters, and distribution/image scripts were skimmed rather than fully audited.
Whether the XXE-enabled default is intentional backward compatibility or a regression is unresolved, and I could not check CVE/advisory metadata (no external lookups allowed).

rejected_leads.lead: SecurityStore field injected into QueueControlImpl (artemis-server/.../management/impl/QueueControlImpl.java lines 85/120/127) and AddressControlImpl (lines 71/81/88) is assigned but never read anywhere in the class, which could indicate that an authorization check for management operations (e.g. QueueControl.moveMessages to an arbitrary otherQueueName, AddressControl operations) was deleted.
rejected_leads.reason: Not enough evidence to raise as a candidate: (a) AddressControlImpl also never reads its managementService field, suggesting long-lived vestigial dependencies rather than a targeted deletion; (b) neither class holds anything that implements SecurityAuth, and SecurityStore.check(...) requires one, so it is unclear what check could have been removed without further code; (c) no upstream copy is available to diff against. Mentioned only as an unconfirmed lead, not submitted.

rejected_leads.lead: Weak randomness for a handshake nonce: NettyConnector.randomBytes/randomNumber use Math.random() (artemis-core-client/.../NettyConnector.java lines 1375-1387) and RandomUtil uses java.util.Random (artemis-commons/.../RandomUtil.java line 28).
rejected_leads.reason: The nonce feeds a client/server HTTP-upgrade echo check, not an authentication or key-derivation boundary, and the pattern is long-standing utility code; no concrete attacker-controlled security impact could be shown.

rejected_leads.lead: STOMP frame handler processes SEND/ACK/SUBSCRIBE without checking connection.isValid() in handleFrame (VersionedStompFrameHandler lines 90-128).
rejected_leads.reason: Counterevidence in source: onSend calls connection.validate() (line 192) and every other path funnels through StompConnection.getSession()/manager.getSession(...), which authenticates the supplied credentials, so an unauthenticated peer cannot send/subscribe. No bypass demonstrated.

rejected_leads.lead: SCRAM login module returns true from login() even when the username/password entry is missing and generates random user data (SCRAMPropertiesLoginModule lines 85-100).
rejected_leads.reason: This is an explicit anti-user-enumeration design (random user data means the SCRAM client proof cannot succeed), and SCRAMServerSASL only reports success when scram.isSuccessful() after proof verification; no bypass found.

rejected_leads.lead: KubernetesClientImpl.buildSSLContext returns a non-initialised SSLContext when the CA file is absent (lines 150-156).
rejected_leads.reason: An uninitialised SSLContext causes HttpClient configuration/use to fail rather than silently trusting all peers, so this is a robustness bug, not a trust bypass; configuration is also operator-controlled.

rejected_leads.lead: Web console/Jolokia and console WAR attack surface (XSS-type issues).
rejected_leads.reason: The console implementation is not in this snapshot (artemis-console only packages the external artemis-console-war artifact), so no console source could be reviewed.

summary: Reviewed the assigned ActiveMQ Artemis 2.40.0-SNAPSHOT source tree (2078 files, main sources only; no test sources present). I navigated with the P1 relation index (2053 indexed files, syntax/call edges only, no control- or data-flow) and verified all leads in source text. I traced the main trust boundaries: core SecurityStore/JAAS authentication and authorization (LDAP, Properties, SCRAM, Kubernetes, BasicSecurityManager, User/password hashing), core-protocol ServerSession checks (send/consume/browse/create/delete), management (ManagementServiceImpl, ArtemisRbacInvocationHandler, ArtemisMBeanServerGuard, AddressControlImpl/QueueControlImpl), the STOMP/OpenWire/AMQP/MQTT protocol handlers, and the shared helpers (XmlProvider, PasswordMaskingUtil, ObjectInputStreamWithClassLoader, CompositeAddress, repository matching). One concrete security weakness is submitted as a candidate with low confidence: XmlProvider's XML-parser hardening is bypassed by default (external entities/DTDs permitted unless `-Dartemis.disableXxe` is set). This is reachable by attacker-supplied XML at least through server-side XPath selector evaluation of message bodies. Because the property semantics are also consistent with intentional backward-compatibility behaviour, I flagged it as a lead rather than a confirmed defect and explicitly recorded the counterevidence. Other plausible-but-unconfirmed leads are listed in rejected_leads.
